title: What adab means
hook: adab is courtesy toward Allah, people and things

segments.voice: Yesterday, despair, and your line: never despair. That closed the diseases of the heart. Did you take the one small step of looking? Day one thousand two hundred ninety-one.

A boy is eating at the Prophet's table, and his hand is wandering all over the shared dish, reaching here, reaching there. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps the moment, told by the boy himself, Umar ibn Abi Salamah, who was being raised in the Prophet's household. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, doesn't scold him or send him away. He gives him three short instructions. And with them, a new part of the path begins: manners, and the word that holds them. Today: adab.
screen: `A HAND ALL OVER THE DISH.` → `NO SCOLDING.` → `ADAB.`

segments.voice: Here's what he told the boy: young man, say the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you. Three instructions at one meal, and they reach in three directions. Saying Allah's name is courtesy toward Allah. Eating from what's in front of you, not reaching across everyone's side, is courtesy toward the people at the table. And the right hand is a habit for the body itself, the way the meal is held. Adab is the word for that whole web: manners, courtesy, the right way to be with Allah, with people, and with things. Second, why it isn't small. The Qur'an praises the Prophet's character in one line, in Pickthall's words: "And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature." On this path, manners aren't decoration on top of faith; they're how character shows up at a table. Third, courtesy reaches past people. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says Allah has prescribed excellence in everything, and gives a hard example: when you slaughter, sharpen the blade and spare the animal. Even there, in that moment, there's a right way. Things and creatures are owed courtesy too. And last, the boy. In al-Bukhari's report, he says that was how he ate from then on. Not a rule memorized. A habit given gently, at the right moment, that stayed.
screen: `SAY THE NAME, RIGHT HAND, NEAR SIDE.` · `TOWARD ALLAH, PEOPLE AND THINGS.` · `OF A TREMENDOUS NATURE.` · then, large: `EXCELLENCE IN EVERYTHING.`

segments.voice: The practice: do one thing courteously. Settle, and breathe. Choose one ordinary thing you'll do today, and decide to do it with adab. A meal: say the name of Allah before it, if that's yours to say, and eat from your own side. A door: hold it, and close it gently. A tool, a plate, a borrowed book: put it back the way you found it, or better. A message: answer it with a greeting first. Picture yourself doing it, slowly, with care. If you pray, you can ask for good manners. The bell holds the time.
Adab. Courtesy and good manners toward Allah, people and things; the right way to do an ordinary thing. Today's word.
Your line: courtesy in everything. Do your one thing with adab today, and notice who or what it touched. Tomorrow, the manners of the tongue: adab of speech. Day one thousand two hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: Muslims learn adab, the manners of daily life, from the Prophet's example: saying bismillah before eating, eating with the right hand and from what is nearest, greeting, and treating people, animals and things with care.
